text:
olivia: Heads-up: planning a 'wavegate' canary for the new CUDA 13.2 driver + NCCL 2.20 kernel on Dedicated today 18:30 UTC. Goal: validate NVLINK stability and network fallback behavior under steady-state KV-cache workloads.

sam: +1. what's the canary surface? region + instance types? :eyes:

olivia: Canary lanes: eu-west1 (h100-dedicated), us-central1 (a100-1x), and ap-southeast1 (mixed). 5% of each region's Dedicated pool, pinned to reserved hosts to avoid autoscaler churn.

chen: Are we doing staged network MTU tests? last time MTU mismatch caused intermittent NCCL timeouts.

olivia: Yes — plan is: 1) deploy driver + NCCL variant to canaries 2) run synthetic all-reduce with incremental message sizes and MTU probe 3) validate app-level metrics (OOMs, NVLINK errors, NCCL timeouts) + infra metrics (link drops, kernel logs) 4) if any gating metric trips, auto-fallback to driver-12.6 image via rollback policy.

marta: Add perf counters for kernel preemption stalls and cudaSanity OOMs. Thresholds?

lee: Suggested gating thresholds: NCCL_TIMEOUTs > 0.2 per 1000 ops, OOMs > 1 per 100k tokens, host link drops > 2 in 10m. Latency p95 increase > 12% triggers manual pause.

sam: What about customer-facing Dedicated customers on latency SLAs? We should ring-fence them.

olivia: Ring-fence yes. Canary only touches discretionary capacity first, not SLA-backed pools. If a customer is on Reserved SLA, they are excluded from this wave.

infra-oncall: oncall will watch metrics and escalate. We'll set a 30m warmup then 2h observation window. If green, proceed to phased waves (20% -> 50% -> global).

chen: Can we have a fallback that keeps model-serving alive by routing to CPU-based fallback or older model variant if GPU nodes temporarily fail?

lee: We already have policy to reroute low-priority traffic to shared-host GPUs or CPU fallback. But must ensure KV-cache TTL fallback doesn't double-charge tokens. Add a cost-tag so ops can see reroute token counts.

marta: Also add a temporary egress rule in the VPC to block jumbo frames if MTU probes cause failures during the canary. We'll toggle via firewall rule named "wavegate-mtu-guard".

sam: rollout command please?

olivia: Here's the deployment snippet we'll use (applied per-region):
```bash
./infra/deploy_wave.sh \
  --region eu-west1 \
  --hosts reserved_h100_waveA \
  --driver nvidia-driver-13.2.0 \
  --nccl nccl-2.20.0-wavegate \
  --canary-percent 5 \
  --auto-rollback "on_gating_fail"
```

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] enqueueing job wavegate-eu-west1-1867205432. status: queued

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] job wavegate-eu-west1-1867205432 -> started on reserved_h100_waveA (hosts: 12)

marta: Running MTU probe now on canaries: probe sizes 1500, 9000, 12000. logging to /var/log/wavegate/mtu-probe.log

chen: tail of latest kernel log from one canary host: 
[2026-11-02T18:34:10Z] nvlink: link reset, lane 2
[2026-11-02T18:34:11Z] nvidia: nvhost_drm: ioctl timeout
[2026-11-02T18:34:12Z] nvlink: training succeeded

lee: I'll correlate that with NCCL trace: 
NCCL INFO rank0 -> rank1: allreduce start
NCCL WARN: timeout 210ms (threshold 200ms)
NCCL INFO: retrying ring

olivia: Those minor warnings expected during initial training. Keep an eye — if we see retries > 0.5% wipe and OOMs, we'll rollback.

infra-oncall: Observability checks added: dashboards 'wavegate/mu-metrics' + alert 'wavegate-gating' with severity P1 if threshold exceeded. Channels: #eng-infra pager + #dedicated-ops.

sam: Do we need to pre-warm KV cache warmers to avoid cold-start spikes when some nodes are in fallback?

marta: Good call. Launching a KV cache warmer job (low-rt priority) now targeting canary hosts; will run for 20m.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] wavegate-eu-west1-1867205432 -> completed step: driver install (12/12 hosts), step time: 4m 12s

chen: Metric snapshot at +25m: NCCL retries 0.18% (ok), host link drops 0, OOMs 0, p95 latency +3%.

lee: That looks good. Proceed to next region after 1h observation.

olivia: Rolling to us-central1 now with a slightly smaller canary (3%). Command same with --canary-percent 3.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] enqueueing job wavegate-us-central1-1867205432. status: queued

sam: Quick reminder — disable automatic scale-up on the canary hosts to avoid extra gpu churn. set autoscaler: disabled for reserved_h100_waveA and reserved_a100_waveB.

marta: Autoscaler disabled for canary host groups. Also tagging canary hosts with "wavegate:1867205432" for billing tracking.

lee: Cost note: if we hit fallback to CPU for >15m, expected incremental cost ~+$1.2k/hour across regions due to cross-zone egress and CPU instances. Flagging for SRE finance sync.

olivia: If any region trips gating, plan is: immediate auto-rollback on region, pause global, notify customers impacted via support-runbook, and run postmortem.

infra-oncall: Observability: alerting configured to auto-open a Zoom incident room if P1 fires. Pager duty escalation on for eng-infra and eng-sre.

sam: Anything else we should add before go?

marta: Add a short smoke test to validate model outputs (sanity prompts) so we can detect subtle quality regressions. We'll push a small eval set to canaries.

olivia: Good — smoke tests added. Launching global coordinator now. Expect phased waves over next 6h if metrics hold. Will update here every milestone. :rocket:

lee: I'll be monitoring NVLINK and NCCL dashboards. ping me if you want manual pause.

chen: Thanks team. I'll watch kernel logs and run extra fuzzing on border frames.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] wavegate-us-central1-1867205432 -> started on reserved_a100_waveB (hosts: 8)

infra-oncall: Standing by.

olivia: Update @here — after 2h observation across both canaries: metrics stable. proceeding to phased 20% wave in eu-west1 and us-central1. ap-southeast1 delayed pending additional NVLINK training tests.

sam: Noted. Keep ap-southeast1 on hold and re-run the jumbo-frame probe with slightly higher inter-packet delay.

marta: Will do. Also starting cost tracking in the finance dashboard under "wavegate/1867205432".

lee: minor note: we saw a single host report an nvlink training retry spike at +70m that self-healed. watching.

olivia: If that persists, we'll mark host for repro and pull logs; don't rollback fleet-wide for a single host.

chen: copying logs to s3://redwood-wavegate-logs/1867205432/host-17/kernel.log

olivia: Thanks. I'll post a short postmortem template in #postmortems if anything escalates. Otherwise, I'll close this thread after global rollout completes.

sam: Great job team. :thumbsup:
